reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is integrating multi-source NBA data (participation, minutes, fouls, shots) into a coherent probabilistic model that accounts for temporal dependence. Static BNs fail because game outcomes are serially correlated. DBNs address this by introducing temporal edges, but require careful specification of the transition kernel to avoid overfitting. The hidden Markov variant further abstracts latent skill levels, useful when direct observation is noisy. These models form a hierarchy: static BN is a special case of DBN with identity transition matrix; DBN reduces to HMM when all observations are conditionally independent given the hidden state. Practical implementation uses conjugate priors for analytical tractability and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) for posterior inference. Cross-validation metrics assess predictive accuracy, while information criteria balance fit and complexity. Limitations include sensitivity to prior choice, computational cost of DBN inference, and the ergodicity assumption that may not hold for playoff teams.
